The CDN shared cache myth — and why self-hosting wins today

The historical argument for serving jQuery/React from a public CDN was "shared browser cache — user already downloaded it from another site." This is false since Chrome 86 (2020): cross-origin resources are cached separately per top-level origin (cache partitioning). There is no shared CDN cache benefit. The tradeoffs are now purely about DNS lookup cost, connection establishment, and control.

Self-hosting advantages
  • Same origin = no DNS lookup + TLS handshake per resource
  • HTTP/2 connection multiplexing with your main origin
  • Full CSP control (script-src 'self' works)
  • Cache control headers you define
  • No GDPR concerns from loading from external domains
  • Availability independent of third-party CDN uptime
Third-party CDN advantages
  • Global edge PoPs closer to users
  • Automatic updates for security patches
  • Zero infrastructure management
  • Useful for: large shared libs where you want team to update centrally
  • Google Fonts (though self-hosting is better for performance)

Connection cost breakdown — same-origin vs new origin

Every new origin costs: DNS lookup + TCP SYN/ACK + TLS 1.3 handshake before the first byte arrives. With HTTP/2, your main origin already has a connection open.

Self-host or CDN — decision matrix

Asset TypeRecommendationReason
App JS bundleSelf-host alwaysCore to your app, needs cache control
CSS framework (Tailwind)Self-host (purged)CDN serves full 3MB, you serve 10KB purged
Fonts (Google Fonts)Self-host WOFF2Cache partitioning kills CDN benefit; privacy
React/Vue runtimeSelf-host (bundled)Already in your bundle; CDN adds extra connection
Icon library (FA)Self-host (tree-shaken)CDN serves all icons; you serve only used ones
jQuery (legacy)CDN acceptableWide use, but cache partition kills shared benefit
Maps (Google Maps SDK)CDN + preconnectToo large to self-host; use resource hints
Video (YouTube embed)CDN + facadeUse lite-youtube-embed until play click

Self-hosting Google Fonts + preconnect fallback

// Step 1: Download fonts locally (use google-webfonts-helper.app)
// Step 2: Serve from /public/fonts/ with immutable cache header

/* styles/fonts.css */
@font-face {
  font-family: 'Inter';
  src: url('/fonts/inter-var.woff2') format('woff2-variations');
  font-weight: 100 900;
  font-display: swap;
}

/* Next.js: next/font — automatically self-hosts Google Fonts at build time */
import { Inter } from 'next/font/google';
const inter = Inter({ subsets: ['latin'], display: 'swap' });
// Next.js downloads Inter at build, serves as static assets — zero CDN calls

/* If you must use a third-party CDN, add preconnect hints */
<!-- HTML -->
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com">
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin>

// Nginx: serve self-hosted assets with long cache + immutable
// location /fonts/ {
//   add_header Cache-Control "public, max-age=31536000, immutable";
// }
